body: https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/blob/2347e56772355691ec1ba1487d06120f3d4a2176/Libraries/LibWeb/HTML/HTMLIFrameElement.cpp#L108 not that it matters too much for webcompat purposes, but we actually have the exact workaround suggested here, but I hadn't gotten around to filing spec issue / fixing yet since there are some other workarounds I hadn't investigated fully yet

Thanks @shannonbooth, good to know!

I asked Claude to look into what Gecko, Chromium, and WebKit do here, and what the options for a spec fix are:

> In the crashtest's case, Gecko, Chromium, and WebKit bail out because the old document lost its window/frame when the iframe navigated:
>
> - Gecko: [`nsFrameLoader::CreateBrowsingContext`](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/751f5671de2d327ff436154dfca6ed1733809163/dom/base/nsFrameLoader.cpp#L294-L298) returns null since the owner document has no inner window. [`MaybeCreateDocShell`](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/751f5671de2d327ff436154dfca6ed1733809163/dom/base/nsFrameLoader.cpp#L2153-L2157) also rejects documents that aren't `IsActive()`, which includes bfcached ones.
> - Chromium: [`HTMLFrameElementBase::DidNotifySubtreeInsertionsToDocument`](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/6ca4e60b94475fa916dfb688608e6cc72693a1bf:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/html_frame_element_base.cc;l=201) returns if the document has no frame; [`FrameLoader::DetachDocument`](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/6ca4e60b94475fa916dfb688608e6cc72693a1bf:third_party/blink/renderer/core/loader/frame_loader.cc;l=1487) shuts down the old document, which clears it.
> - WebKit: [`HTMLFrameElementBase::postConnectionSteps`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/1617fd34a2bcaacaf5bc22fac66ce1a73b8d620b/Source/WebCore/html/HTMLFrameElementBase.cpp#L170-L171) returns if the document has no frame; [`Document::willBeRemovedFromFrame`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/1617fd34a2bcaacaf5bc22fac66ce1a73b8d620b/Source/WebCore/dom/Document.cpp#L3738) detaches it on navigation.
>
> All three only put top-level pages in bfcache ([Gecko](https://github.com/mozilla-firefox/firefox/blob/751f5671de2d327ff436154dfca6ed1733809163/docshell/base/CanonicalBrowsingContext.cpp#L3429), [Chromium](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/6ca4e60b94475fa916dfb688608e6cc72693a1bf:content/browser/renderer_host/render_frame_host_manager.cc;l=1433), [WebKit](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/1617fd34a2bcaacaf5bc22fac66ce1a73b8d620b/Source/WebCore/loader/FrameLoader.cpp#L2536-L2541)), so an iframe's own navigation destroys its previous document. The spec allows that, since _intendToKeepInBfcache_ in [unload a document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#unload-a-document) is up to the user agent. So this is reachable in a user agent that keeps such documents, or for a document in a bfcached page that script can still reach (e.g., from an opener).
>
> Options:
>
> 1. Return early from the `iframe` and `frame` post-connection steps if the node document isn't fully active. `object` already checks this when determining what it represents, and so does `embed`'s "potentially active". This matches Ladybird and Gecko's `IsActive()` check.
> 2. Require _intendToKeepInBfcache_ to be false for child navigables' documents, to match browsers. Then traversing back within an iframe repopulates the entry instead of reusing the document, since destroying it sets the entry's document to null. That doesn't cover documents in a bfcached page, so 1 seems needed either way.
